messages:
ashwin: Heads up — after yesterday's release we saw a short-lived but sharp compile backlog and a p50 latency bump on small-batch traffic. compile_queue_len spiked to ~220 for ~10m.

maria: saw the same on canary at ~02:13 UTC. QPS steady but compile-rps jumped and kernel picks changed.

kevin: quick tail from the node that hit the highest queue: 
```text
[02:12:02] compile_queue_len=218
[02:12:02] compile_rps=85
[02:12:02] chosen_kernel=matmul_tile64x64
[02:12:02] fallback_kernel=matmul_tile32x32
```

sasha: that kernel is fine for long sequences, but autotune flipping to tile64 for small-seq workloads is suspicious. new batching-window heuristic landed in the same release — could be feeding the wrong hist.

ashwin: I profiled the request batches. live seq-dist suddenly reported median=24 (was ~6). prefix KV cache evictions jumped; prefix_cache_miss_rate -> 37% during the spike. Suggests reordering/coalescing increased lifetimes and evicted hot prefixes.

ci-bot: perf-test-smallbatch (PR #4819) failed: p50 latency +12% vs baseline. Full logs: https://ci.example/1234

maria: trying a local repro now.

kevin: repro command I used: 
```bash
./bench --model redwood-3b --concurrency 30 --seq-len 32 --batch-hint small
```

sasha: confirmed repro on my laptop container with same flags. bisect candidates: last 5 merges touched batching and autotune selector. @ashwin can you run git-bisect on infra/runtime to narrow?

ashwin: starting bisect. quick hypothesis: batching-window default change altered observed histogram fed to autotune, causing autopick to prefer larger-tile kernels for small-batch traffic.

ashwin: interim test — I reverted batching-window default to 8 on canary, metrics normalized within ~6m: compile_queue_len -> ~8-12, compile_rps dropped to baseline, p50 latency returned to prior. Rolling hotfix hold in progress.

maria: great triage. Do we need to revert autotune change too, or add a guard?

kevin: autotune algorithm is fine for large seqs. Plan: add safety-clamp: never switch to a larger tile kernel if current live-seq distribution has >70% of requests under small-seq threshold. Also add a cooldown window after any kernel swap.

sasha: also proposing a compile-backoff policy: if compile_queue_len > 50, prefer cached fallback kernels and delay noncritical compile picks. That should avoid backpressure and KV churn.

ashwin: filing follow-ups: 1) revert batching default in release branch, 2) autotune safety clamp + cooldown, 3) compile-backoff feature + unit and perf e2e tests. Marking as P0/rollback-blocker for this rollout.

ashwin: created issues: https://issues/RT-789 (batching revert), https://issues/RT-790 (autopick clamp), https://issues/RT-791 (compile backoff).

maria: deployed hotfix to prod hold and removed rollout-blocker label from the release after confirming metrics. Keep this monitored for 24h :thumbsup:

kevin: I'll take the autotune patch. sasha, can you draft the compile-backoff design? we should include metrics we'll alert on (compile_queue_len, compile_rps, kv_evictions, smallseq_median).

sasha: on it. I'll post a short design doc and perf test matrix tomorrow morning.

ashwin: thanks all. lessons: don't let batching histogram changes feed autotune without a safety check, and think defensively about compile storm backpressure -> KV churn.
